options: ① The girls who are wearing pants are dancing.
② The girls who are wearing skirts are dancing.
③ The girls, who are wearing skirts, are dancing.
④ The girls, who are wearing pants, are dancing.
⑤ The girls, who are wearing pants, are not dancing.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계대명사의 한정적 용법과 계속적 용법의 의미 차이를 이해하고 있는지 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 24. 다음 중 바르게 쓰인 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: 'I lied to my mom, who made her angry' (who->which여야 함), 'This is Gimchi, many foreigners...' (which 빠짐), 'Mike sent me flowers which...' (옳음), 'Sumi is reading a book..., where...' (사물 선행사 목적격이므로 which여야 함). 맞는 것은 'Mike sent me flowers which touched my heart' 하나뿐으로 보이나, 출제 의도에 따라 다를 수 있음. 통상 1~2개.
sentences: · He has a sister, that runs a cafe.
· I lied to my mom, who made her angry.
· This is Gimchi, many foreigners want to eat.
· Mike sent me flowers which touched my heart.
· Sumi is reading a book about Korea, where she visited three years ago.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계대명사와 관계부사의 혼용, 계속적 용법의 격과 제약 등을 꼼꼼히 따져야 하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 <보기>에서 어법상 옳은 것만을 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ 계속적 용법 who(옳음), ⓑ 앞 문장 수식 which(옳음), ⓓ 부모님을 기쁘게 한 사실 which(옳음). ⓒ 콤마 뒤 that 불가, ⓔ it 중복 삭제 필요, ⓕ president를 수식하므로 which가 아닌 who가 적절함.
sentences: <보기>
ⓐIt was Ron, who always supported me.
ⓑHe lied to his mom, which made her angry.
ⓒThe book, that Mike lent me, is very interesting.
ⓓJane won a gold medal, which pleased her parents so much.
ⓔI want to see the Mona Lisa, which Leonardo da Vinci painted it.
ⓕAbraham Lincoln was the 16th president of the USA, which freed slaves.
questions.reason_for_classification: 계속적 용법의 여러 쓰임 중 옳은 것을 선별하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 26. 다음 중 밑줄 친 부분의 쓰임이 어색한 것은?
questions.explanation: ② '엄마에게 거짓말을 했다'는 사실이 엄마를 화나게 한 것이므로 사람이 아닌 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 받는 which가 와야 합니다.
options: ① I have a twin sister, <u>who</u> runs a bakery.
② I lied to my mom, <u>who</u> made her angry.
③ Jane won a gold medal, <u>which</u> pleased her parents.
④ The book, <u>which</u> Mike lent me, is very interesting.
⑤ I'll borrow the book from Tom, <u>who</u> has read it many times.
questions.reason_for_classification: 계속적 용법의 관계대명사가 가리키는 대상(선행사)에 따른 적절한 관계사 선택을 묻습니다.

questions.question: 27. 다음 관계대명사의 설명을 바탕으로 작성한 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 흐름과 어법상 가장 적절한 문장을 모두 고르면? (2개)
questions.explanation: ⓒ 태양은 유일한 존재이므로 제한할 필요 없이 부가 정보를 주는 계속적 용법이 적절함. ⓓ 특정 호텔을 지칭하므로 제한적 용법이 적절함. ⓐ는 민호가 이미 특정된 인물이므로 콤마가 있는 계속적 용법이 더 자연스러우며, ⓑ는 school에 콤마가 필요하고, ⓔ는 어느 남자인지 묻는 질문에 대한 답이므로 한정적 용법이어야 합니다.
sentences: 제한적 용법의 관계대명사는 ‘identification’의 기능을 수행합니다. 즉, 선행사의 범위를 좁혀(narrow down) 한정 지을 때 사용합니다. 반면, 계속적 용법의 관계대명사는 선행사의 범위를 좁힐 필요가 없거나, 맥락상 대화 참여자들이 이미 알고 있는 대상에 대해 추가적인 정보를 제공하는 경우에 사용합니다.
ⓐ Minho who used to be in the army now works at a bank.
ⓑ Last weekend, she told me about her new school which she likes very much.
ⓒ The sun, which is one of millions of stars in the universe, provides us with heat and light.
ⓓ I stayed at the hotel that my friend recommended.
ⓔ The man, who is living next door to Mary, is cool.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계대명사의 제한적 용법과 계속적 용법의 기능적 차이를 상황 맥락에 적용하는 능력을 묻는 고난도 문제입니다.

questions.question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓓ 중 흐름과 어법상 옳은 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: ⓐ Art Golding이라는 특정 인물이므로 계속적 용법이 적절함(옳음). ⓑ Supernova라는 특정 영화이므로 계속적 용법이 필요한데 that을 썼음(틀림). ⓒ film star를 특정하므로 콤마 없는 한정적 용법이 문맥상 더 자연스러울 수 있음. ⓓ 한정적 용법으로 그날 밤 본 영화임을 나타냄(옳음). ⓐ, ⓓ 2개가 옳습니다.
sentences: Breaking News: Art Golding Dies
ⓐ The actor Art Golding, who starred in films such as ‘Tornado’ and ‘Iceberg’, has died after a long illness.
ⓑ Art Golding’s most famous film was ‘Supernova’, that broke all box-office records.
ⓒ The film star, who played the ship’s captain in ‘Iceberg’.
ⓓ It’s the film we saw on TV the other night.
questions.reason_for_classification: 지문 흐름 속에서 한정적/계속적 용법의 적절성을 판별하는 문제입니다.

questions.passage:
We all know that a diet which contains a variety of foods keeps our bodies healthy. But sometimes we are not sure which foods are good for which body parts. Nature, however, gives us a big clue. Look at the following examples. Each of these foods not only looks like a certain body part but is also good for that body part.
Slice open a tomato and compare it with the human heart. You will see that they look similar. They both have multiple hollow spaces and are red. Researchers say that the chemicals which make tomatoes red are good for your heart and blood. In addition, eating tomatoes can lower your risk of heart disease.
Look at the shape of a walnut. Do you notice anything? Yes, it’s very similar to the shape of the human brain! A walnut is divided into two parts, just like the brain. Walnuts also have wrinkles, which the brain has too. Studies show that walnuts help our brains stay healthy and active. They are also good for preventing Alzheimer's disease.
A slice of carrot looks like the human eye. ⓐ<u>Carrots have some chemicals that can make vitamin A, which improves your vision</u>. It helps your eyes process light and send a clear image to the brain. So if you want healthy eyes, eat carrots.
Cutting onions is not fun because it makes you cry. But try slicing one anyway. You can see that the inside looks a little like a human cell. Scientists say that onions contain vitamin B, which helps make new, healthy cells.
Now, let’s move on to ginger. ⓑ<u>What body part come to mind when you see it</u>? Doesn’t it look like a stomach? You may not like ginger’s strong taste or smell, ⓒ<u>but these come from a special chemical that prevents you from feel sick and throwing up</u>. For this reason, ginger can be good for your stomach.
ⓓ<u>Isn’t it amazed that some foods (A)(mirror) the body parts that they are good for?</u> ⓔ<u>Interestingly, there is many other such foods</u>. Find as many as you can and try to eat a variety of them.
questions.question: 29. 위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ vitamin A를 선행사로 하여 vision을 개선한다는 부가 설명을 하는 계속적 용법 which와 수 일치가 모두 올바릅니다. ⓑ come -> comes, ⓒ feel -> feeling, ⓓ amazed -> amazing, ⓔ is -> are.
questions.reason_for_classification: 교과서 본문 기반의 문법 복합 문제입니다.

questions.question: 30. 다음 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 빈칸에 which가 들어갈 수 있는 문장을 모두 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ 앞 문장 수식 계속적 용법(which), ⓒ 사물 선행사 목적격(which/that), ⓔ 계속적 용법 목적격(which). ⓑ 의문사 how, ⓓ 가주어-진주어 접속사 that, ⓕ 명사절 접속사 that. 따라서 ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓔ가 들어간 ②번이 정답입니다.
sentences: ⓐJohn said nothing, __________ made me angry.
ⓑI didn't know __________ Mike solved the puzzle.
ⓒIt is the necklace __________ my mom made for me.
ⓓIt is amazing __________ Mary cooked all this food by herself.
ⓔThe book, __________ Mike lent me, is very interesting.
ⓕIt is thought _________  getting enough sleep is good for health.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계대명사(계속적/한정적)와 접속사, 의문사의 쓰임을 구별하는 종합 문제입니다.

questions.passage:
Thor knew something was wrong. His wife's beautiful golden hair was gone. He knew only Loki could do such a terrible thing. ⓐ<u>Thor found Loki, which did not take so long</u>.
"You'd better undo what you did, or you'll be sorry." Thor said angrily to Loki. ⓑ<u>Loki, who was scared, promised that he would get golden hair for Thor's wife</u>. ⓒ<u>Loki knew that this terrible thing could be fixed by Ivaldi's sons, who could make fine golden hair</u>. He went to them and said,
"I heard Brokk and his brother are the finest smiths. Is that true?"
"No, we are the finest smiths," the sons of Ivaldi replied. ⓓ<u>Loki made them angry at Brokk, who was what Loki wanted.</u>
Loki said, "They're making three treasures for Odin, Thor, and Frey." ⓔ<u>He also told vald's sons that they should make better treasures, which seemed to be an interesting bet</u>
"Of course we can," they answered.
questions.question: 31. 위 글의 흐름에 근거하여 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법의 적절한 쓰임에서 가장 거리가 먼 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ에서 Loki는 사람이므로 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로 which가 아닌 who를 써야 문법적으로 더 적절합니다(문장 전체 수식이 아닌 Loki를 찾는 것이 오래 걸리지 않았다는 맥락이면 who). 다만 맥락상 'Loki를 찾는 것' 자체면 which도 가능하나 인칭 선행사와의 결합을 묻는 의도인 듯합니다. ⓓ의 Brokk 또한 사람이므로 who가 와야 합니다.
questions.reason_for_classification: 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 선행사와 관계사 매칭의 적절성을 평가합니다.

questions.question: 32. 관계부사를 이용하여 두 문장을 한 문장으로 바꿀 때 가장 올바른 것은?
questions.explanation: ② 날짜(day)를 선행사로 하여 when으로 연결이 잘 되었습니다. ① 이유가 아니므로 when이 적절함. ③ the way와 how는 함께 쓸 수 없음. ④ where를 썼으면 뒤의 대명사 there를 삭제해야 함. ⑤ reason for this why는 중복 표현임.
options: ① I miss the summer. In the summer, we used to go to the beach. -> I miss the summer why we used to go to the beach.
② Leah will never forget the day. Her dog joined her family then. -> Leah will never forget the day when her dog joined her family.
③ I make peanut sauce in some way. I showed it to my class mates. -> I show my classmated how I make peanut sauce in some way.
④ Felix bought this cupcake at the cafe. I want to stop by there. -> I want to stop by the cafe where Felix bought this cupcake there.
⑤ Eden hasn’t come home yet. I want to know the reason for this. -> I want to know the reason for this why Eden hasn’t come home yet.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사(when, where, how, why)의 올바른 사용과 제약 사항을 평가합니다.

questions.question: 33. 어법상 옳은 것만을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: (a) the way 또는 how 하나만 써서 옳음, (d) 가주어-의미상주어(for)-진주어 구문으로 옳음, (f) too ~ to 구문으로 옳음. (b) us가 와야 함, (c) bought의 목적어가 없으므로 where가 아닌 which가 와야 함, (e) 성격 형용사가 아니므로 for Jessica가 와야 함.
sentences: (a) He regrets the way he lived his life.
(b) It won’t be easy for we to win the game.
(c) This is the house where my aunt bought last year.
(d) It was great for Richard to rest for two weeks.
(e) It is necessary of Jessica to make such a decision.
(f) The movie was too difficult for me to understand.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사, 부정사의 의미상 주어, too~to 구문 등 중3 필수 어법의 정확성을 종합적으로 평가합니다.

questions.question: 34. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 관계사 중에 같은 말이 들어가는 것으로 짝지어진 것은? (that은 제외함)
questions.explanation: ⓑ which/that, ⓙ which/that으로 같은 관계사가 들어갑니다. ⓐ where, ⓒ who, ⓓ where, ⓔ who/that, ⓕ whose, ⓖ whose, ⓗ who/that, ⓘ whose.
sentences: ⓐ This is the city _________ I grew up.
ⓑ Look at the car _________ I want to buy.
ⓒ I have a friend _________ loves to travel.
ⓓ The building _________ I work is very tall.
ⓔ The dog _________ barked all night kept me awake.
ⓕ This is the school _________ reputation is excellent.
ⓖ I met a woman _________ daughter goes to my school.
ⓗ The singer _________ performed at the concert was amazing.
ⓘ The woman _________ car was stolen reported it to the police.
ⓙ The office _________ she saw in the advertisement looked impressive.
questions.reason_for_classification: 선행사와 뒷문장 구조에 따른 다양한 관계사(관계대명사, 관계부사, 소유격)를 선별하는 문제입니다.

questions.passage: Turkey is a country ⓐ[where / when] East meets West, so it has a long tradition of trade. It is a natural place for large markets like the Grand Bazaar. The market was ⓑ[building / built] in 1455 in Istanbul. Back then, the market had two big buildings, and people traded goods like cloth and gold there.Today the Grand Bazaar is much bigger, and it is the largest ⓒ[covering / covered] market in the world. It has 64 streets and more than 4,000 shops under one roof. The market attracts over 250,000 visitors every day. You can buy almost any imaginable item there.If you visit the market, ask shop owners if they carry nazar boncuğu, a traditional Turkish symbol for good luck. Also, if you want a nice snack, make sure to try lokum, a traditional Turkish candy.
questions.question: 35. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ의 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 말을 선택하여 바르게 짝지은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ 장소 선행사 country를 수식하므로 where, ⓑ 시장은 '지어지는' 수동의 의미이므로 built, ⓒ 지붕으로 '덮인' 시장이므로 covered가 적절합니다.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사, 수동태, 분사의 형용사적 용법을 지문 문맥에 적용하는 문제입니다.

questions.passage: ⓐ <u>터키는 동양과 서양이 만나는 나라이고</u>, so it has a long tradition of trade. It is a natural place for large markets like the Grand Bazaar. The market was built in 1455 in Istanbul. Back then, the market had two big buildings, and people traded goods like cloth and gold there.Today the Grand Bazaar is much bigger, and it is the largest covered market in the world. It has 64 streets and more than 4,000 shops under one roof. The market attracts over 250,000 visitors every day. You can buy almost any imaginable item there.Extra Tip: Ask shop owners if they carry nazar boncuğu, a traditional Turkish symbol for good luck. Also, if you want a nice snack, make sure to try lokum, a traditional Turkish candy.
questions.question: 36. 밑줄 친 ⓐ의 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 ①~⑤의 단어들을 바르게 배열하여 문장을 완성할 때, ★에 올 단어는?
questions.explanation: Turkey is a country where East meets West의 순서로 배열됩니다. 두 번째 빈칸(★)에는 where가 옵니다.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사를 포함한 문장 배열 능력을 평가합니다.

questions.question: 37. <보기> 중에서 어법상 옳은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ 전치사+관계대명사(in which)가 관계부사 where 역할을 함(옳음), ⓓ 시간 선행사 time과 when(옳음), ⓔ 장소 선행사 bakery와 where(옳음). ⓑ reason 뒤에는 why가 와야 함, ⓒ library 뒤에는 where가 와야 함.
sentences: <보기>
ⓐ This is the town in which I was born.
ⓑ Tell me the reason where you hate Sue.
ⓒ This is the library when I met her for the first time.
ⓓ Don't forget the time when you should leave for the train.
ⓔ Is this the bakery where Uncle Ben buys bread every Saturday?
questions.reason_for_classification: 선행사와 관계부사의 짝이 올바른지 판단하는 문제입니다.

questions.passage: One key factor to understand why a team performs well (a)<u>is</u> their work culture. This means the team enjoys their workplace and (b)<u>likes </u>working together. Work culture includes the values, ethics, attitudes, and beliefs that (c)<u>shape</u> how an organization operates daily. Who creates this environment? The leader does. Whether (d)<u>leading </u>a big or small team, leaders can shape the work culture by setting up systems that guide behavior and attitudes. They create a space (e)<u>when</u> team members can develop their skills through meaningful and challenging work, increasing productivity in a happy environment.
questions.question: 38. 윗글의 (a)~(e) 중에서, 어법상 어색한 것은?
questions.explanation: (e)의 선행사 a space는 장소의 개념이므로 관계부사 when이 아니라 where가 오는 것이 적절합니다.
questions.reason_for_classification: 문맥에 맞는 관계부사(where vs when)를 구별하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 39. 어법상 옳지 않은 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: ⓐ reason 뒤에 for which 또는 why가 와야 하며 he came이라는 절이 오므로 for는 부적절함. ⓓ big enough for us가 되어야 함. 나머지 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ, ⓕ는 관계부사의 생략 및 부정사 구문으로 옳음. 따라서 2개가 틀렸습니다.
sentences: ⓐ Do you know the reason for he came?
ⓑ My father doesn't like the way I drive.
ⓒ It took 5 minutes for me to get here.
ⓓ The pizza was big enough of us to share.
ⓔ We should find a place where we can be safe.
ⓕ It is very thoughtful of them to prepare the present for him.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사와 부정사의 의미상 주어 등 여러 핵심 문법의 오류를 찾아내는 복합 문제입니다.

questions.question: 40. 주어진 조건에 따라 문장을 완성할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말이 나머지와 다른 것은?
questions.explanation: ① which (built의 목적어), ② which (전치사 for의 목적어), ③ which (계속적 용법), ⑤ which (전치사 in의 목적어). ④는 뒷문장이 완전하고 장소를 나타내므로 where가 들어갑니다.
options: ① That is the house ____ they built last year.
② This is the reason for ____ I like horror movies.
③ We visited the Louvre Museum, ____ is in Paris.
④ Is this the factory ____ your father is working?
⑤ Do you know the country ____ the great poet was born in?
sentences: 조건: that은 사용할 수 없음, 빈칸은 1단어
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계대명사(목적격, 주격)와 관계부사 where를 문장 구조 분석을 통해 구별하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 41. 빈칸에 'that'이 들어갈 수 없는 것은?
questions.explanation: ③ 전치사(in) 뒤에는 관계대명사 that을 사용할 수 없습니다. 이 경우 which를 써야 합니다.
options: ① The girl ____ I'm waiting for is your sister.
② This is the singer ____ I really wanted
③ Do you remember the bank in ____ I worked?
④ The eggs ____ I bought yesterday smell bad.
⑤ I love the puppy ____ my grandfather gave to me.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계대명사 that의 제약 사항(전치사 뒤 사용 불가)을 평가합니다.

questions.question: 42. 다음 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 표현으로 옳은 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 장소 선행사 office 뒤의 where, (B) 이유 선행사 reason 뒤의 why, (C) 방법의 how (the way how는 불가하므로 how만 사용).
sentences: • Is this the office (A)__________ David is working?
• I want to know the reason (B)__________ he hates me.
• Tom never shows (C)__________ he solves the problem.
questions.reason_for_classification: 기초적인 관계부사 선별 문제입니다.

questions.question: 43. 다음 중 어법상 어색한 문장은?
questions.explanation: ③ reason 뒤에는 why가 오거나 for which가 와야 하며, in which는 이유의 의미로 쓰이지 않습니다.
options: ① Please tell me how you made the doll.
② Spring is when everything comes alive.
③ He didn't say the reason in which he was absent.
④ The place where the president will stay is confidential.
⑤ Is this the restaurant where we can eat popular Mexican foods?
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사를 전치사+관계대명사로 전환할 때 적절한 전치사 사용 여부를 묻습니다.

questions.question: 44. 다음 우리말 해석에 맞게 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 문장을 완성하시오.
questions.explanation: '순간(the moment)'을 선행사로 하여 관계부사 when을 사용한 문장을 완성합니다.
sentences: 나는 내가 처음으로 자전거를 탔던 순간을 잊을 수가 없다.
(can't / first / moment / time / when / the)
questions.answer: I can't forget the moment when I rode the bicycle for the first time.
questions.reason_for_classification: 주어진 단어를 활용하여 관계부사가 포함된 문장을 영작하는 서술형 문제입니다.

questions.question: 45. 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장의 번호를 괄호 안에 쓰고 문장 전체를 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.explanation: ③ house 뒤의 문장이 완전하지 않거나 장소 개념이면 where가 적절하며, held의 목적어가 아닌 장소를 나타내므로 where 또는 in which가 되어야 함. ④ what 뒤에 전치사의 목적어(to)의 대상이 빠져있으나 for가 어색함.
sentences: ① Spring is when everything comes alive.
② I can't forget the day on which we met.
③ This is the house which my birthday party was held.
④ The presents were what I looked forward to my birthday.
questions.answer: 3) (③) → This is the house where my birthday party was held.
questions.reason_for_classification: 문장 오류를 찾아 올바른 관계부사나 관계대명사 구문으로 고치는 능력을 평가합니다.

questions.passage:
Why We Buy What We Buy
Have you ever wondered ___ⓐ___ you've bought things that you don't even want or need? Let's consider ___ⓑ___ affects us ___ⓒ___ it comes to buying things.
㉠<u>Why do I want to buy that my friends bought?</u>
㉡<u>Jeff goes to the shopping center and sees a pair of soccer shoe in display</u>. He recognizes the shoes (㉮) a glance because more than half of the boys on his soccer team wear them. Although he already has many pairs of soccer shoes, he ends up buying another new pair.
We can use the "bandwagon effect" to explain Jeff's behavior. ㉢<u>A bandwagon is a wagon in a parade which encourages people to jump aboard and enjoy the music</u>. Ⓐ<u>As</u> more and more people get on the bandwagon, others are more likely (㉯) get on or follow it. ㉣<u>In this way people tend to buy something just because other people have bought.</u>
Why do I buy a pair of pants and a bag after I have bought a new coat?
Lisa buys a coat that she really loves. Immediately, she realizes that her pants do not match her new coat. So, she buys new pants that go perfectly (㉰) her new coat But she sees that none of her bags match her new clothes. So, she buys a new bag. Most of her money is spent (㉱) buying the new items to complete her new look.
㉤<u>What made Lisa to search for new items immediately after buying a new coat</u>? The "Diderot effect" may explain it. Denis Diderot, a French writer, received a new gown as a gift. Soon after receiving the gift, he noticed that all of his furniture did not go well (㉲) his new gown. So, he ended up replacing most of it. The Diderot effect, therefore, is the concept that purchasing a new item often leads to more unplanned purchases.
questions.question: 46. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에 들어갈 단어가 바르게 짝지은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ 이유를 묻는 why, ⓑ 주어 역할을 하는 의문사 what(무엇이), ⓒ 'when it comes to(~에 관해서라면)' 관용 표현의 when이 적절합니다.
questions.reason_for_classification: 간접의문문의 의문사와 관용적인 부사절 접속사의 쓰임을 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 47. 다음 주어진 두 문장을 관계부사를 이용하여 한 문장으로 고쳐 쓰시오.
questions.explanation: 'the way'와 'how' 중 하나만 사용하거나 'the way that' 또는 'the way in which'로 써야 합니다.
sentences: <보기>
• I didn’t know the way.
• Tom solved the puzzle in the way.
questions.answer: I didn’t know how Tom solved the puzzle. (또는 I didn't know the way Tom solved the puzzle.)
questions.reason_for_classification: 방법을 나타내는 관계부사의 특수한 제약 사항을 적용하여 문장을 결합하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 48. 다음 중 어법상 맞는 문장을 있는 대로 모두 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ how 명사절(옳음), ⓒ reason why에서 why 생략(옳음), ⓓ day that(관계부사 대용) (옳음), ⓖ day we start... on (on의 목적어가 빠진 구조로 옳음), ⓗ day when (옳음). ⓑ where가 필요함, ⓔ for why는 틀림, ⓕ place where여야 함, ⓘ way 뒤에 how나 which는 어색함.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사와 관계대명사의 다양한 용법 중 옳은 것을 가려내는 종합 평가 문제입니다.

questions.question: 49. 다음 밑줄 친 부분의 어법상 쓰임이 나머지와 다른 것은?
questions.explanation: ③의 when은 앞의 선행사 day를 수식하는 관계부사입니다. 나머지 ①, ②, ④, ⑤의 when은 모두 '~할 때'라는 의미의 시간 부사절 접속사입니다.
options: ① Please call me when you leave.
② I loved English when I was a student.
③ Sunday is the only day when I can relax.
④ You should plan your schedule well when you go on a trip.
⑤ It’s not good to stay up all night when you study for an exam.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사 when과 부사절 접속사 when의 용법을 구분하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 50. 다음 ⓐ~ⓘ 중 어법상 옳은 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: ⓑ the way S+V(옳음), ⓕ 가주어-진주어 that(옳음), ⓖ 가주어-진주어 that(옳음). ⓐ on 삭제 필요, ⓒ it 삭제 필요, ⓓ who owns 필요, ⓔ which was painted 필요, ⓗ doing -> do, ⓘ for 삭제 필요. 총 3개가 옳습니다.
sentences: ⓐ I remember the day when she left town on.
ⓑ I don’t like the way you stare at me.
ⓒ Jinsu found a wallet on the street, which he took it to the police station right away.
ⓓ Mr. Clinton, owns many companies, is very rich.
ⓔ This is Sunflowers, which painted by Vincent van Gogh.
ⓕ It is not surprising that humans use all their five senses.
ⓖ It is great that you want to spend time with your granddaughter.
ⓗ It is dangerous to doing outdoor activities on heavy rainy days.
ⓘ The birthday presents were the reason why I looked forward to my birthday for.

Cancun is a city ___(A)___ 4.8 million tourists travel every year. One of the most popular activities to do there is looking at the area's beautiful sea life underwater. However, tourist activities are seriously damaging parts of the sea near Cancun.

They made an underwater museum away from the places ___(B)___ sea life was dying. It's about 14 meters below the surface and contains 500 statues.
The statues are made from materials ___(C)____ support sea life. They provide additional places for plants and animals to live on. Over time, many types of sea life will grow on the statues, ___(D)____ will make the artwork unique. The artists want people to see a variety of sea life on the statues. buildings need air conditioning, which uses a lot of energy and contributes to climate change. (다)<u>That's why architects in Singapore have begun to design eco-friendly buildings what use less air conditioning but are still cool inside</u>.
(라)<u>For example, many buildings in Singapore designed to have an open structure</u>. This structure makes it possible for outside air to move throughout a building. This natural air flow is how these buildings stay cool. In addition to making open structures, architects add large gardens. questions.question: 1. (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말로 올바른 것은?
questions.explanation: (A)와 (B)는 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오고 장소를 나타내는 선행사를 수식하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하고, (C)는 주격 관계대명사 that, (D)는 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 받는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
questions.answer: ③

questions.question: 3. 위 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 올바른 것을 두 개 고르면? (정답 2개)
questions.explanation: ⓐ는 옳은 문장이다. ⓑ도 'travel to' 전치사를 포함한 목적격 관계대명사 구문으로 옳다. ⓒ는 주어가 'One'이므로 'is'가 되어야 하고, ⓓ는 'places for'가 자연스럽다. ⓔ는 간접의문문 어순에 따라 'how rich sea life is'가 되어야 한다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 두 문장을 한 문장으로 고쳐 썼을 때, 어법상 바른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'the way in which'는 선행사와 관계부사를 대체하는 전치사+관계대명사로 옳다. ⓒ 'the place which ... in'은 전치사 in의 목적어가 선행사이므로 옳다. ⓓ 'the month when'은 시간의 관계부사로 옳다.
sentences: ⓐ I remember the time. + He went there at that time. → I don’t remember when he went there to.
ⓑ Tell me the way. + She came here in the way. → Tell me the way in which she came here.
ⓒ Do you know the place? + The old man lived there. → Do you know the place which the old man lived in?
ⓓ July is the month. + We take the final test in the month. → July is the month when we take the final test.
ⓔ 2021 was the year. + I entered this school then. → 2021 was the year which I entered this school.
ⓕ I want to visit the place. + He bought the place last year. → I want to visit the place where he bought last year.
questions.answer: ③
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사와 '전치사+관계대명사'의 전환 및 적절한 관계사 선택을 묻는다.

questions.question: 5. 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장을 바르게 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓒ reason why, ⓔ day on which (또는 when), ⓕ country which... in (또는 where)은 모두 문법적으로 옳다. ⓐ는 which가 아닌 when이나 in which가 와야 하고, ⓑ는 on이 불필요하며, ⓓ는 where 뒤에 in이 오면 안 되고, ⓖ는 way how를 같이 쓸 수 없다.
sentences: ⓐ Spring is the season which we go on a picnic.
ⓑ That is the house which they built last year on.
ⓒ I explained the reason why I left the party early.
ⓓ New York has many hotels where we can stay in.
ⓔ She can’t forget the day on which she got a prize.
ⓕ Do you know the country which the poet was born in?
ⓖ He understands the way which his mom cooked for him.
questions.answer: ⑤
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사 where, when, why와 그 대체형인 '전치사+관계대명사'의 정확한 사용법을 묻는다.

questions.question: 6. 대화의 내용에 맞도록 노르웨이에 관한 홍보물에 들어갈 표현을 영작하시오.
questions.explanation: 조건에 따라 'that'을 제외한 관계부사 'when'을 사용하고, 주어진 단어를 조합하면 'Visit Norway when the sun never sets!'가 된다. (Norway를 장소로 볼 경우 where도 가능하나, 보통 '해가 지지 않는 시기'에 초점을 맞추어 when을 선호함)
sentences: <조건>
• that을 제외한 관계부사를 반드시 사용할 것
• 다음 단어 중 필요한 단어를 한 번만 사용하여 영작할 것 (필요시 변형 가능)
( always / cycle / hike / never / night / set / summer / sun / the )
questions.answer: Visit Norway when the sun never sets
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사를 사용하여 완전한 문장을 영작하는 문제로, 관계사절의 구조를 이해해야 한다.

questions.question: 7. 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓔ 'the reason why'는 선행사 reason과 관계부사 why가 적절히 쓰였다. ⓐ는 'how to use', ⓑ는 주어와 목적어가 같으므로 'ourselves', ⓒ는 'tries to talk', ⓓ는 'ends up arguing'이 되어야 한다.

questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사 why와 동명사 관용표현, 재귀대명사 등을 변별하는 문제이다.

questions.question: 8. 다음 선행사 및 관계사의 활용이 문법적으로 옳은 문장만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ way that(가능), ⓑ season when(가능), ⓓ library that ... at(가능), ⓔ reason (why)생략(가능). ⓒ 'where my sister painted red'는 painted의 목적어가 빠진 불완전 문장이므로 where 대신 which가 와야 하고, ⓕ 'office where his crew decorated' 또한 decorated의 목적어가 없으므로 which가 와야 한다.
sentences: ⓐ That’s the way that I play baseball.
ⓑ Spring is the season when the flowers bloom.
ⓒ I went into the room where my sister painted red.
ⓓ This place is the library that Tim can study for the exam at.
ⓔ That’s the reason we see the different colors of a rainbow.
ⓕ He walked into the office where his crew decorated for Christmas.
questions.answer: ④
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사와 관계대명사의 뒷문장 완전성 여부를 정확히 판단해야 하는 고난도 문제이다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 두 문장을 관계부사를 활용하여 한 문장으로 만들었을 때 ★에 오는 단어는?
questions.explanation: 두 문장을 합치면 'The winter when I traveled in Canada was very cold.'가 된다. 단어 순서대로 나열하면 'The(1) winter(2) when(3) I(4) traveled(5) in(6) Canada(7) was(8) very(9) cold(10)'이므로 6번째 오는 단어 ★은 'in'이다.
sentences: 1. The winter was very cold.
2. I traveled in Canada then.
(내가 캐나다를 여행했던 그 겨울은 매우 추웠다.)
questions.answer: ①
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사를 사용하여 문장을 합성하고 특정 위치의 단어를 찾는 문제이다.

questions.question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓑ 'traditional market where I can buy all kinds of food at'에서 관계부사 where 뒤에는 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데 전치사 at의 목적어가 비어있다. 따라서 where를 which로 바꾸거나 at을 삭제해야 한다.
sentences: Tomorrow is Parents’ Day. ⓐ<u>Parents’ Day is the day on which we give thanks to our parents</u>. I want to do something special for my parents. ⓑ<u>I’m going to go to the traditional market where I can buy all kinds of food at</u>. I’ll prepare a nice dinner for my parents. ⓒ<u>But I don’t know how I should cook</u>. ⓓ<u>Also I want to know where I should buy groceries at reasonable prices</u>. ⓔ<u>That’s the reason why I have to call my grandmother</u>.
questions.answer: ②
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사 where와 전치사의 중복 사용 오류를 찾아내는 문제이다.

questions.question: 11. 다음 두 문장을 관계부사를 활용하여 한 문장으로 만들었을 때 (C)에 들어갈 단어는?
questions.explanation: 'There was a moment when everybody was very quiet.'에서 A:when, B:everybody, C:was, D:very, E:quiet 순이므로 (C)에는 'was'가 들어간다.
sentences: 1. There was a moment.
2. Everybody was very quiet then.
→ There was a moment ( A ) ( B ) ( C ) ( D ) ( E ). (모두가 매우 조용했던 순간이 있었다)
questions.answer: ①
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사를 이용한 문장 연결 및 어순 파악 능력을 묻는다.

questions.question: 12. 다음과 같이 답한 학생의 점수는?
questions.explanation: 1:O(the way s v 가능하므로 학생 틀림), 2:X(on that 불가하므로 학생 맞음), 3:X(where 뒤 대명사 중복 불가하므로 학생 맞음), 4:O(how절 가능하므로 학생 맞음), 5:O(the way in which 가능하므로 학생 틀림), 6:X(when과 then 중복 불가하므로 학생 맞음), 7:X(reason why... for에서 for 중복 불가하므로 학생 맞음). 맞은 문항은 2, 3, 4, 6, 7번으로 총 5점이다.
sentences: 문장이 어법상 옳으면 O, 틀리면 X로 표시하시오.
(3)학년 (15)반 번호(1) 이름 (김OO)
문항 | 문제[각 1점] | 답안
1 | I don't know the way he came into the room. | X
2 | I can remember the day on that we met first. | X
3 | This is the room where he hid his toys in there. | X
4 | He must change how he acts and talks in this way. | O
5 | He is satisfied with the way in which he lived his life. | X
6 | Do you remember the day when we went to a movie then. | O
7 | I don't know the reason why he was absent from school for. | O
questions.answer: ⑤
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계부사 관련 여러 문법적 오류를 복합적으로 판단하여 점수를 계산하는 고난도 문제이다.

English has often borrowed words from other cultures or languages. Here are some examples with interesting stories.
shampoo
ⓐThe word shampoo comes from the Hindi word chāmpo, that means "to press." In India, the word was used for a head massage. British traders in India experienced a bath with a head massage and introduced it to Britain in the 18th century.
ⓑThe meaning of the word shampoo changed a few times after it first entered English around 1762. In the 19th century, shampoo got its present meaning of "washing the hair." Shortly after that, the word began to be also used for a special soap for the hair.
robot
ⓒThe word robot comes from the play R.U.R., which wrote in 1920 by a Czech writer Karel Čapek. In the play, robots are machines that look like humans. They are designed to work for humans and are produced in a factory.
ⓓIt is interesting that the idea of using the word robot didn't come from Karel Čapek. He originally called the machines in his play labori from the Latin word for "work." However, his brother suggested roboti, which means "slave workers" in Czech. Karel Čapek liked the idea and decided to use the word roboti. ⓔIn 1938, the play was made into a science fiction show on television in Britain.

questions.question: 23. ⓐ~ⓔ중 어법상 틀린 것의 개수는?

questions.question: 24. 다음 중 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⑤ 'if or not'은 병치해서 쓸 수 없으며, whether or not으로 고쳐야 합니다. ② 또한 주어절에서는 if를 쓸 수 없습니다. (복수 정답 가능성이 높으나 전형적인 if 제약은 ⑤입니다)
options: ① I don't know if she understood what I was trying to say.
② If we go to the beach or stay home depends on the weather forecast.
③ He questioned if the project which was planned carefully would be completed on time.
④ If they catch the early train, they'll arrive in time to see the sunset over the ocean.

questions.reason_for_classification: 명사절 접속사 if의 구조적 제약(or not과 바로 병치 불가)을 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 25. 다음 우리말을 영어로 바꾸어 쓸 때 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 5단어로 쓰시오. (미래형 사용하지 말것)

questions.question: 26. 밑줄 친 'if'의 의미가 나머지와 다른 하나는?
questions.explanation: ①은 조건(~라면)의 부사절이며, 나머지는 간접의문문(~인지)의 명사절입니다.
options: ① I'll buy you a new computer <u>if</u> you pass the test.
② I wonder <u>if</u> she is good at basketball.
③ I am not sure <u>if</u> he will come here.
④ He couldn't tell <u>if</u> she went out.
⑤ Do you know <u>if</u> he's married?

questions.question: 27. 어법상 옳은 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: 옳은 문장은 1, 2, 4, 5번입니다. 3번은 rains로, 6번은 Whether ... is not certain으로 고쳐야 합니다.
sentences: I wonder if he is smart.
Give her this book if you see her.

questions.passage:
Laughter is human. We laugh out loud when we see funny things, hear ①<u>interesting something</u> or ②<u>feel joyfully</u>. We laugh even in our writings, such as emails or texts, as we do in our conversations. How do we do that?
"Ha-ha" is a form of written laughter. Everyone knows ③<u>what does it mean</u> and how to use it. Actually. ④<u>it had been used</u> since long ago until now. Even Shakespeare used "ha-ha" in his works.
Another form of written laughter is LOL. It stands for "Laughing Out Loud." People also use ROFL a lot, which means "Rolling On the Floor Laughing. These expressions have become popular because they can type quite quickly.
XD also represents laughter in text. It shows a laughing face with a mouth open and eyes closed tightly. XD is not a word. It's an emoticon, which is a group of letters or symbols used to represent a facial expression. The emoticon XD expresses our happy feelings more visually than ha-ha and LOL do.
These days, people use - a "face with tears of joy." This is a small picture called an "emoji." Lots of laughing emojis are available to use online, so people can express their laughter in a variety of ways.
Some emojis have grown bigger and some even move or make laughing sounds.
Laughing marks can represent our facial expressions and delivers our voice tones. By using various laughing marks, ⑤<u>we can show our friends how much we care for them</u>. Laugh, even in written forms, and your friends will laugh with you.

questions.question: 10. 다음 문장을 간접화법으로 바꾸어 쓸 때 어법상 옳은 것은? (2개)

questions.question: 34. [C]의 밑줄 친 문장의 의미와 일치하도록 <보기>에서 주어진 단어를 적절히 배열하여 쓰시오.
questions.explanation: help + 목적어(you) + (to) get used to~ 구조를 사용하여 문장을 완성함.
sentences: <보기> you, get, help
It will _______________ used to the sound of the language.
questions.answer: help you get
questions.reason_for_classification: 준사역동사 help의 목적격 보어 형태(동사원형)를 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 35. <보기>의 문장 중 어법상 올바른 것을 모두 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓑ get + to부정사, ⓓ get + 목적어 + p.p.(cut은 p.p.형태 동일), ⓔ had + 목적어 + p.p.(준비된)가 옳음. ⓐ had + 목적어 + p.p.(cleaned), ⓒ had + phone + fixed(p.p.), ⓕ had + face + drawn(p.p.)으로 고쳐야 함.
sentences: <보기>
ⓐ Lucy have her dog cleaned.
ⓑ I got him to decorate the room.
ⓒ I had my phone fixed the man.
ⓓ Why don't you get your hair cut?
ⓔ Mom had the dinner prepared before everyone came.
ⓕ The woman had her face drown by the painter.
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사/get의 목적격 보어에서 목적어와의 능동/수동 관계에 따른 형태(to부정사, 동사원형, 과거분사)를 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.passage: After his death. the two sons took their share of the father's wealth and settled in different cities. Five years passed. Puru, who had been following his father's words carefully. had no money left. But his brother was richer than ever. Puru was puzzled about where he had gone wrong, so he visited Puneet to find out. Puneet welcomed Puru with open arms. That night, when the brothers sat down to chat after dinner. Puru asked the question that had been on his mind for days. "I followed our father's advice, but I am not happy. I built a house in every city. But because I could not always stay there. I hired people and had them look after the house. Father said we should sleep comfortably and enjoy our food, so (A) <u>I had experts design my bed and a great chef prepare my meals. </u>He told us to spend like a rich man, so I bought what I wanted without worrying about money. But look at me now! I am empty-handed. Did you not follow our father's wisdom? Tell me, brother, how did you get so rich?"
questions.question: 36. 윗글의 (A)와 같은 의미를 가진 문장은?
questions.explanation: (A)는 '능동' 사역문(전문가가 침대를 디자인하게 하다)이므로, 이를 목적어와 보어의 수동 관계(내 침대가 전문가에 의해 디자인되게 하다)인 'had + 목적어 + p.p.' 형태로 바꾼 5번이 의미가 같음.
options: ① I had experts prepare my meals and a great chef design my bed.
② I had a great chef design my meals and experts prepare my bed.
③ I had my meals prepared by experts and my bed designed by a great chef.
④ I had my bed prepared by experts and my meals designed by a great chef.
⑤ I had my bed designed by experts and my meals prepared by a great chef.
questions.reason_for_classification: 5형식 사역동사 구문에서 능동 형태를 수동 형태(목적격 보어로 과거분사 사용)로 전환하는 능력을 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.passage:
The manager let us ㉠<u>painting</u> anything we wanted. We decided to paint cute things because the wall was near an elementary school. We divided into three groups and began ㉡<u>to paint</u>. I was in the group with Minsu and Jiwon. I chose my spot and ㉢<u>start</u> to paint my favorite movie character. Minsu painted some flowers and Jiwon did some background drawings.
Our club painted ㉣<u>about for</u> five hours. After we finished, we got together and shared the day's experiences. Minsu was very proud of his flower painting. He said, "My flower is so real that a bee landed on it." I said, "Drawing on a wall was ㉤<u>a lot</u> harder than drawing on paper."
We all agreed that our wall painting wasn't perfect. But it didn't matter. (가) 우리는 우리의 동네를 조금 더 밝고 더 행복하게 만들었어. We didn't just paint pictures on a wall that day. It was a better tomorrow (나)that we painted.
questions.question: 37. ㉠~㉤ 중 어법상 옳은 것을 모두 고르면?
questions.explanation: ㉡ begin은 to부정사와 동명사 모두 목적어로 취하므로 옳음. ㉤ 비교급 강조 부사 a lot은 적절함. ㉠ paint(사역동사 보어), ㉢ started(시제 일치), ㉣ for about(어순)으로 고쳐야 함.
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사의 목적격 보어, 비교급 강조 부사, 동사의 시제 일치 등 여러 문법 요소를 점검하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 38. 어법상 옳은 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: 옳은 문장: 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 (5개). 3번은 got my sister 'to help', 7번은 makes my brother 'open'으로 고쳐야 함. (단, 문제의 선택지에 5개가 없으므로 재검토: 'had to'는 조동사이므로 제외하면 4개일 가능성 있음.)
sentences: ・ He had to clean his room yesterday.
・The dentist had me open my mouth.
・ I got my sister help me to do the dishes.
・ He helped the old lady to cross the street.
・ Jennie helps her friends do their homework.
・ Peter sometimes lets his dog sleep in his bed.
・ My grandpa makes my brother to open the window.
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사, 준사역동사(help, get)의 목적격 보어 형태를 정확히 알고 있는지 묻는 개수 파악 문제입니다.

questions.question: 39. 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
questions.explanation: 사역동사 have + 목적어 + 동사원형 + get along with(~와 잘 지내다) 구문을 조합하여 작성함.
sentences: 그들의 선생님들은 그들이 그들의 친구들과 잘 지내라고 시키신다.
<조건>
・ 동사는 'have'를 사용할 것
・'along'을 한 번 사용할 것
・ 9~10단어의 완전한 문장으로 쓸 것
questions.answer: Their teachers have them get along well with their friends.
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사 have의 문장 구조와 관용 표현을 조건에 맞춰 영작하는 능력을 테스트하는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 40. 다음 글을 읽고 글의 흐름에 맞게 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸을 완성하시오.
questions.explanation: (A)는 '건물에 들어오게 하다'이므로 let us enter, (B)는 '가방을 열어보게 하다'이므로 have us open bags로 구성함.
sentences: <보기>
make, let, have, enter, bags
The White House is open to public tours. However, the guards will (A)________ _________ ________ ________ the building if we don’t have an ID card.
Also, they can (B)________ ________ ________ ________ ________ before going into the building for safety reasons. It means we should not carry anything inside the building.
questions.answer: (A) let us enter (B) have us open our bags
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사의 문맥상 적절한 선택과 그에 따른 보어 형태(동사원형)를 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.passage:
In sports, only the players get a trophy or medal, but they don‘t win on their own. There are people who help the players. These people are often (A)<u>hide</u> and don‘t get attention. However, they are as (B)<u>important</u> as the players. Here are some examples.
Pacers in Marathon
Pacers run with other runners and lead them in a marathon. Pacers are experienced runners, and their job is to help other runners (C)<u>manage</u> their race better. There can be several pacers in a race. Each pacer runs at different speeds and finishes the race in different times. Pacers usually have flags or balloons (ⓐ)<u>show</u> their finish time. Runners can choose a pacer depending on their target finish time. For example, if a runner (ⓑ)<u>want</u> to finish the race in four hours, the runner will follow the four-hour pacer. Since the pacer keeps track of the time, the runner can achieve his or her goal of finishing the marathon in a particular time more (ⓒ)<u>easy</u>. In short,
pacers run but they don‘t run to win. They run for others.
questions.question: 41. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(C) 단어의 올바른 형태로 연결된 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 수동의 의미이므로 과거분사 hidden, (B) as ~ as 사이에는 형용사 원급 important, (C) help의 보어이므로 (to) manage가 적절함.
options: ② hide		more important		to manage

questions.question: 42. 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓒ 단어의 올바른 형태로 연결된 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ balloons를 수식하므로 현재분사 showing, ⓑ 주어가 단수이므로 wants, ⓒ 동사(achieve)를 수식하므로 부사 easily가 적절함.

questions.question: 43. 다음 중 문법적으로 옳은 문장은?
questions.explanation: ⑤ 사역동사 made + 목적어 + 동사원형으로 적절함. ① had(사역)은 to fix를 fix로, ② makes(사역)은 feeling을 feel로, ③ let(사역)은 slept를 sleep으로, ④ have(사역)는 we를 us(목적격)로 고쳐야 함.
options: ① I had him to fix my watch yesterday.
② She makes me feeling like a little girl.
③ The teacher didn't let him slept in class.
④ Our parents have we go to bed early at night.
⑤ Ms. Kim made Mina introduce herself to her classmates.
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사의 목적격 보어 형태와 목적어의 격 일치를 종합적으로 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 44. 다음 중 어법상 옳은 것은? (정답 2개)
questions.explanation: ② have + 사람 + 동사원형, ⑤ get + 사람 + to부정사로 모두 옳음. ① laptop은 사용되는 것이므로 used, ③ last night이므로 made, ④ professional accountant는 관리하는 주체이므로 take care of(원형)로 써야 함.
options: ① My brother let his laptop use for his friend.
② They will have repairman fix the water pipes tomorrow.
③ Matilda makes her husband wash the dishes last night.
④ He had the professional accountant taken care of the taxes.
⑤ Linda is getting a hair stylist to dry her hair after the perm.
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사/get의 능동 및 수동 목적격 보어 형태를 구별하는 고난도 문제입니다.

questions.question: 45. 다음 중 어법상 옳은 것은?
questions.explanation: ① get + 목적어 + p.p.(수리된) 구조로 옳음. ② ironed(다려진), ③ to buy(get+to), ④ go out(let+원형), ⑤ throw(get+to/사역이 아니면 to부정사)로 고쳐야 함.
options: ① Hanni got her watch repaired.
② Minji is having her shirts iron.
③ Hyein got her mother buy a T-shirt.
④ Haerin let her sister going out this weekend.
⑤ Sarah got her mom throw a party for her birthday.
questions.reason_for_classification: 목적어와의 관계에 따른 목적격 보어의 형태(과거분사 vs 동사원형/to부정사)를 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.passage: Yesterday, my computer broke down, so I couldn't do my homework. It made me (A)[feel / to feel] worried. (가)_________, my brother let me (B)[use / to use] his portable computer. While I was doing my homework, Mom had my computer (C)[fix / to fix / fixed].
questions.question: 46. 위 글의 (A)~(C)에 알맞은 표현을 괄호 안에서 골라 바르게 묶인 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 사역동사 make+원형(feel), (B) 사역동사 let+원형(use), (C) 사역동사 had+목적어+수동보어(fixed)가 적절함.
options: ② feel		to use	     to fix
④ to feel	to use	     fix
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사의 능동적 보어와 수동적 보어(과거분사)를 동시에 묻는 문제입니다.

questions.question: 47. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 어법상 옳지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: want는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하며, 사역동사와 같은 동사원형 보어(clean)는 취할 수 없음.
options: ③ the park a better place
④ his son to go to the grocery store
⑤ his students clean the classroom walls
sentences: James wants to make                               .
questions.reason_for_classification: 5형식 문장에서 동사의 종류(make)에 따라 올 수 없는 목적격 보어 형태를 찾는 문제입니다.

questions.passage:
ⓐ<u>Comfort food is food that makes you feeling good</u> when you are sad, angry, or ______ stressed out. ⓑ<u>It can also make you think of happy moments from the past</u>. It satisfies not only the stomach but also the heart. Comfort foods differ around the world. Let's see ⓒ<u>what comfort foods do our international readers enjoy</u>.
Jessica from USA
My comfort food is chicken soup. In the USA, people eat this soup when they have a cold. When I was a small child, I caught a very bad cold. ⓓ<u>My father made me a bowl of chicken soup so that I could get well</u>. The hot soup warmed my body, and I slowly started to feel better. It was also very tasty. Now, when I catch a cold, I eat chicken soup.
Maria from Brazil
In Brazil, ⓔ<u>there are many dishes that made with cassava</u>, a vegetable similar to a potato. I love cassava chips the most. Once when I had a bad day at school and felt stressed out, my best friend bought me a bag of cassava chips. When I started to eat the chips, my stress suddenly disappeared. ⓕ<u>The crisp sound of eat chips made me feel better</u>. Now, every time I'm stressed out, I eat cassava chips. Then I feel good again!
questions.question: 48. 위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 옳은 것만 골라 묶은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓑ make + 원형, ⓓ so that + 주어 + can 구조로 옳음. ⓐ feel, ⓒ what comfort foods our international readers enjoy, ⓔ are made, ⓕ eating으로 고쳐야 함.
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사, 간접의문문 어순, 목적의 부사절(so that), 수동태 등 지문 내 여러 어법을 복합적으로 평가합니다.

questions.passage:
Simon from France
I have many comfort foods, but I love madeleines the most. A madeleine is a small cake that looks like a sea shell. People in France enjoy madeleines as an afternoon snack. My grandmother always makes madeleines for me when I visit her. They taste best when they come right out of the oven. Then the kitchen is filled with a sweet smell. I especially like eating her orange madeleines with a cup of tea. Every time I see or smell madeleines, I think of my grandmother.
(A)<u>네가 오렌지 마들렌을 만들 수 있도록 그녀의 특별한 조리법을 너와 공유하게 해줘</u>. Maybe madeleines will become a comfort food for you!
questions.question: 49. 위 글의 밑줄 친 (A)를 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 이용하여 (B)의 빈칸에 맞게 영작할 때, 필요하지 않은 것을 모두 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: 문장은 'Let me share her special recipe with you so that you can make orange madeleines.'가 되며, 'as'와 'to'는 사용되지 않음.
sentences: (A) 네가 오렌지 마들렌을 만들 수 있도록 그녀의 특별한 조리법을 너와 공유하게 해줘.
<보기>
special / me / make / so / you / orange / let / as / to / her / recipe / madeleines / share / you / that
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사 let 구문과 목적을 나타내는 부사절 접속사 so that을 결합하여 영작하는 문제입니다.

questions.passage:
My name is Yeji. I'm an ocean scientist.
Ocean science is a big field. ⓐ<u>I study oceans and the creatures that live in it</u>. Among other things, ⓑ<u>I have been studying many kind of fish living in the seas near Korea</u>. ⓒ<u>Especially, the growth ring in a fish is interested me</u>. By looking at it, ⓓ<u>I can discover when and where was the fish born</u>.
All the information I get from fish ⓔ<u>can be used to manage the oceans better</u>. My job is important because it makes the best use of nature possible.
questions.question: 1. 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 올바른 것은? [4.2점]
questions.explanation: ⓔ의 'can be used'는 '사용될 수 있다'라는 의미의 수동태로 조동사(can)와 함께 쓰인 어순과 형태가 적절함.
questions.reason_for_classification: 수동태의 기본 형태와 조동사가 포함된 수동태의 쓰임을 묻는 문항임.

questions.question: 2. 주어진 우리말에 맞게 영작하시오. [2점]
questions.explanation: '어디 있는지'는 간접의문문으로 '의문사+주어+동사' 어순인 'where it is'를 사용함.
sentences: (그것이 어디 있는지 나는 모른다.) I should ask her to help me find it.
questions.answer: I don't know where it is.
questions.reason_for_classification: 의문사가 있는 의문문이 문장의 일부로 들어갈 때의 어순을 묻는 간접의문문 문항임.

questions.question: 3. 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
questions.explanation: ②번 문장에서 'who'는 의문사이자 주어이므로 '의문사+동사' 어순인 'who moved'가 간접의문문으로 올바름.
options: ① I wonder how many you read books.
② I don't know who moved my cheese.
③ Do you know where is my hometown?
④ Do you think who invented the camera?
⑤ I don't remember when did the girl finish her work.
questions.reason_for_classification: 문장 내에서 목적어 역할을 하는 간접의문문의 어순과 의문사가 주어인 경우의 특수성을 묻는 문항임.

questions.question: 4. 다음 두 문장을 한 문장으로 만드시오.
questions.explanation: (1) '인지 아닌지'는 if/whether를 사용하며, (3) imagine은 의문사가 문두로 나가지 않음.
sentences: <조건>
(1), (2)번은 ‘or not’을 문장 속에 포함하여 완성하시오.
(1) Can you tell me + Is he honest?
(2) I want to know + Does she work for a law firm?
(3) Do you imagine + What does the monster look like?
questions.answer: (1) Can you tell me if [whether] he is honest or not? (2) I want to know if [whether] she works for a law firm or not. (3) Do you imagine what the monster looks like?
questions.reason_for_classification: 의문사가 없는 의문문의 간접의문문 전환 시 if/whether의 사용과 의문사가 있는 경우의 어순 변화를 묻는 문항임.

questions.question: 5. 괄호 안의 단어를 배열하여 주어진 우리말을 영어로 옮길 때, 다섯 번째로 올 단어는?

Another form of written laughter is LOL. It stands for "Laughing Out Loud." People also use ROFL a lot, which means "Rolling On the Floor Laughing. These expressions have become popular because they can type quite quickly.
XD also represents laughter in text. It shows a laughing face with a mouth open and eyes closed tightly. XD is not a word. It's an emoticon, which is a group of letters or symbols used to represent a facial expression. The emoticon XD expresses our happy feelings more visually than ha-ha and LOL do.
These days, people use - a "face with tears of joy." This is a small picture called an "emoji." Lots of laughing emojis are available to use online, so people can express their laughter in a variety of ways.

questions.question: 48. 위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중 어법상 옳은 것만 골라 묶은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓑ 사역동사 make + 동사원형 think, ⓓ so that 주어 can 구문은 옳음. ⓐ feeling -> feel, ⓒ 어순 오류, ⓔ that are made, ⓕ eating.
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사의 보어 형태와 접속사 so that의 쓰임을 지문 내에서 파악하는 문항임.

questions.passage:
Simon from France
I have many comfort foods, but I love madeleines the most. A madeleine is a small cake that looks like a sea shell. People in France enjoy madeleines as an afternoon snack. My grandmother always makes madeleines for me when I visit her. They taste best when they come right out of the oven. Then the kitchen is filled with a sweet smell. I especially like eating her orange madeleines with a cup of tea. Every time I see or smell madeleines, I think of my grandmother.
(A)<u>네가 오렌지 마들렌을 만들 수 있도록 그녀의 특별한 조리법을 너와 공유하게 해줘</u>. Maybe madeleines will become a comfort food for you!
questions.question: 49. 위 글의 밑줄 친 (A)를 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 이용하여 (B)의 빈칸에 맞게 영작할 때, 필요하지 않은 것을 모두 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: "Let me share her special recipe with you so that you can make orange madeleines."로 영작되며 'as', 'to'는 불필요함.
sentences: (A) 네가 오렌지 마들렌을 만들 수 있도록 그녀의 특별한 조리법을 너와 공유하게 해줘.
<보기> special / me / make / so / you / orange / let / as / to / her / recipe / madeleines / share / you / that
questions.reason_for_classification: 사역동사 let의 사용과 목적을 나타내는 부사절 접속사 so that을 활용한 영작 문항임.

questions.passage: Today everything went wrong. First, I got up late. (㉠) I arrived at school, class had already begun. I quietly sat down at my desk. (㉡) I realized that I had left my report at home. ㉢ my teacher asked me to read my report. I had never been in such a situation, so my face got really red. I want to forget everything about today!
questions.question: 1. ㉠~㉢에 들어갈 단어로 올바르게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.explanation: ㉠은 '~했을 때'의 When, ㉡은 문맥상 '곧'을 나타내는 Soon, ㉢은 '갑자기'를 뜻하는 Suddenly가 자연스럽다.

questions.question: 2. 다음 중 어법상 어색한 문장은?
questions.explanation: 'for a week before doctor'는 전치사/접속사 구조가 어색하며, 문맥상 '의사를 만나기 전'을 의미하려면 'before I saw a doctor' 혹은 'before seeing a doctor' 등이 적절하다.
options: ① We left right after the concert ended.
② Aishah had never seen snow until last year.
③ He had just taken a bath when the phone rang.
④ I've been sick for a week before doctor.
⑤ I had lost my keys, so I couldn't get into my room.
questions.reason_for_classification: 과거완료(had p.p.)와 다양한 접속사(after, until, when)의 쓰임을 묻는 문제로, 전치사구와 접속사절의 구조적 결함이 있는 선택지를 찾는 문제이다.

questions.question: 3. 다음 ⓐ~ⓔ의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: Unless는 'if ~ not'의 의미를 이미 포함하고 있으므로, Unless you don't가 아니라 Unless you work처럼 긍정문으로 써야 한다.
sentences: - ⓐ<u>Unless</u> you don’t work much harder, you won’t pass the exam.
- Before you leave, you should check ⓑ<u>whether</u> all lights were switched off.
- Every student made a noise ⓒ<u>until</u> the teacher came in.
- Jenny was listening to music ⓓ<u>while</u> she was doing her homework.
- I’m sure you will like her ⓔ<u>once</u> you meet her.
questions.reason_for_classification: 접속사 unless가 부정의 의미를 내포하고 있어 중복 부정을 피해야 한다는 문법 규칙을 평가한다.

questions.question: 4. 다음 두 문장을 의미 변화 없이 한 문장으로 연결할 때 어색한 것은?
questions.explanation: Jason이 매우 경험이 많음에도 불구하고 좋은 직장을 찾지 못한다는 '양보'의 의미가 되어야 하므로 Although/Even though가 적절하다. Once는 '일단 ~하면'이라는 뜻이다.
options: ① He turned the lights off. So we couldn’t see anything. → As he turned the lights off, we couldn’t see anything.
② I’ll go to France. I’ll visit the Louvre Museum then. → When I go to France, I’ll visit the Louvre Museum.
③ I like her paintings. But I don’t like her personality. → While I like her paintings, I don’t like her personality.
④ Jason is very experienced. But he can’t find a good job. → Once Jason is very experienced, he can find a good job.
⑤ I didn’t answer all the questions. But I passed the exam. → I passed the exam in spite of not answering all the questions.
questions.reason_for_classification: 여러 가지 접속사(as, when, while, once)와 전치사(in spite of)의 의미를 문맥에 맞게 사용하는 능력을 묻는다.

questions.passage:
(가) One night in February, and earthquake hit. I had gone to bed (A)[since / before] it occurred, and woke up suddenly because my bed was shaking. I thought my brother was shaking my bed ㉠<u>as</u> a joke. But ㉡<u>then</u> I heard the mirror on my desk fall to the floor and break into pieces. I knew it wasn’t my brother then, but I still don’t know what exactly happened.
(나) ㉢<u>Soon</u> the whole room began to shake violently, and Ⓐ<u>my confusion</u> turned to panic. My mom shouted that it was an earthquake and ran into my room. ⓐ<u>I didn’t know how should I react</u>. (B)[As / Though] it was my first time experiencing an earthquake, I just kept saying, “What should I do?”
(다) My mom pulled me and my brother out of bed. We ran to the kitchen and crawled under the table. I could see the light swinging violently and books falling to the floor. ⓑ<u>Our family picture dropped from the wall and the glass covered it broke</u>. A cup tipped over and rolled off the kitchen table. ⓒ<u>Every second, I could hear something else in the apartment breaking</u>. I started to worry that the building would collapse.
(라) ⓓ<u>Then the shaking seemed stopped</u>. We started crawling toward the door. At that moment, my mom’s cell phone rang. It was my dad, who was coming home from work.
He shouted, “It stopped! Get out of the building! Take the stairs! Don’t take the elevator! Hurry!” “Where are you? Are you okay?” my mom asked urgently. My dad answered. “Don’t worry. I’m Okay. I was driving home when the shaking started. But I pulled over immediately. I’m listening to the radio right now to find out what’s going on.”
(마) We nervously made our way down the stairs and outside. I looked around. Parts of buildings had fallen and had smashed several cars. We went to Ⓑ<u>an open space</u> to avoid more falling pieces. How could all this have happened in a few minutes?
(바) (C)[Since / Even though] I had done many earthquake drills in school, I had never thought I’d experience a real earthquake. I still get scared ㉣<u>when</u> I remember that night. I can’t forget the panic that I felt when the furniture was shaking and things were falling to the floor. ㉤<u>After</u> that night, I began to take earthquake drills seriously. ⓔ<u>I realized that I should be prepared for the next earthquake, that can occur at any time</u>.
questions.question: 5. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ㉠~㉤ 중 아래 밑줄 친 단어와 문장 속에서의 어법상 역할이 같은 것은?
questions.explanation: 보기의 unless는 부사절을 이끄는 접속사이다. ㉣의 when 역시 '~할 때'라는 시간을 나타내는 부사절을 이끄는 접속사로 쓰였다.
sentences: Jisu can’t watch TV unless she finishes her work.
questions.reason_for_classification: 접속사의 기능을 식별하는 문제로, 부사절을 이끄는 접속사(when)와 보기(unless)의 역할을 비교한다.

questions.question: 6. 다음 <보기>의 접속사로 완성할 수 없는 문장은? (중복사용 가능)
questions.explanation: ④번 문장은 '예림이가 이 마을로 이사한 지 2년이 되었다'는 뜻이 되어야 하므로 since(~이래로)가 필요하지만 보기에는 as, until, unless, before, although만 있다.
options: ① ________ it was very hot outside, I ate hotteok.
② He changed a lot ________ he got older and older.
③ ________ I think about the wildfire, I still get scared.
④ ________ It has been two years ________ Yerim moved to this town.
⑤ Jisun can’t watch TV ________ she finished her homework.
sentences:
<보기>
as / until / unless / before / although
questions.reason_for_classification: 주어진 한정된 접속사 목록 중 문맥에 맞는 것을 골라 넣는 문제로, 보기 목록에 없는 since의 쓰임을 묻고 있다.

questions.question: 7. 다음 <보기> 중 어법상 옳은 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: ⓒ(과거완료), ⓓ(시간 조건 부사절 현재시제)가 옳다. ⓐ는 four-story building, ⓑ는 불완전한 절, ⓔ는 Five hundred children이다.
sentences:
<보기>
ⓐOur school has a four-stories building.
ⓑWhen we graduated from Gochon Middle School.
ⓒI lost the pen that my friend had bought for me.
ⓓWhen you finish reading the book, I will borrow it.
ⓔFive hundreds children are born in the city every day.
questions.reason_for_classification: 과거완료, 수사 표현, 복합 형용사, 부사절 시제 등 다양한 문법 요소를 종합적으로 묻는 문제이다.

questions.question: 8. ⓐ~ⓖ 중 어법상 올바른 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓕ 5개가 옳다. ⓔ는 spend time on(전치사 누락 혹은 관계사절 구조), ⓖ는 during 대신 while이 쓰여야 한다.
sentences: Students, please check items on the list that are true for you.
Are you addicted to your smartphone?
ⓐ I feel very uncomfortable without my smartphone.
ⓑ I take my smartphone when I go to the bathroom.
ⓒ It is more enjoyable for me to spend time on my smartphone than with friends.
ⓓ I often check SNS postings while studying.
ⓔ I try to reduce the time that I spend my smartphone, but I always fail.
ⓕ I check my smartphone right after I hear the sound of an alert.
ⓖ I have my smartphone next to me during I'm eating.
questions.reason_for_classification: 비교급, 가주어-진주어, 분사구문, 전치사 vs 접속사(during/while) 등 중3 수준의 문법을 종합 판단해야 한다.

questions.question: 9. 다음 빈칸 ⓐ-ⓒ에 들어갈 말이 순서대로 연결된 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ 기간(three hours) 앞이므로 for, ⓑ 기간(twenty minutes) 앞이므로 for, ⓒ 시점(August, 2014) 앞이므로 since가 적절하다.
sentences: ○ She has been cleaning her house _ⓐ_ three hours.
○ They have been studying _ⓑ_ twenty minutes.
○ He has been living here _ⓒ_ August, 2014.
questions.reason_for_classification: 현재완료 계속 용법에서 기간(for)과 시작 시점(since)을 구별하는 기초 문법이다.

questions.passage: What happens ⓐ<u>when</u> you walk backward while you are carrying a cup of coffee?" Han Jiwon, a Korean high school student, did research on this topic- in 2015. (A)<u>Is this project good enough to win a Nobel Prize</u>? Maybe not. But how about an Ig Nobel Prize? He won one in 2017 for this fun research.
questions.question: 10. 다음 중 윗글 속 밑줄 친 ⓐwhen과 쓰임이 다른 것은?
questions.explanation: 본문의 when은 '~할 때'를 의미하는 접속사이다. ⑤의 When은 '언제'를 뜻하는 의문사이다.
options: ① My mouth is watering <u>when</u> I bite a lemon.
② I loved math <u>when</u> I was at school.
③ <u>When</u> we have a cold, we blow our noses very often.
④ He gets upset <u>when</u> he is kept waiting.
⑤ He said to me <u>"When</u> do we meet together?“
questions.reason_for_classification: 접속사 when과 의문사 when의 용법을 구분하는 문제이다.

questions.passage: What happens ⓐ<u>when</u> you walk backward while you are carrying a cup of coffee?" Han Jiwon, a Korean high school student, did research on this topic- in 2015. (A)<u>Is this project good enough to win a Nobel Prize</u>? Maybe not. But how about an Ig Nobel Prize? He won one in 2017 for this fun research.
questions.question: 11. 다음 중 윗글의 밑줄 친 문장 (A)를 같은 의미를 가진 문장으로 올바르게 바꿔쓴 것은?
questions.explanation: '형용사 + enough + to부정사'는 'so + 형용사 + that ~ can' 구문으로 전환할 수 있다.
options: ① Is this project too good to win a Nobel Prize?
② Is this project so good that it cannot win a Nobel Prize?
③ Is this project too good that it cannot win a Nobel Prize?
④ Is this project not good that it cannot win a Nobel Prize?
⑤ Is this project so good that it can win a Nobel Prize?
questions.reason_for_classification: enough to 구문과 so ~ that can 구문의 상호 전환을 묻는 문제이다.

questions.question: 12. 다음 중 밑줄 친 부분을 올바르게 바꾼 것을 두 개 고르면?
questions.explanation: ②는 If절을 분사구문(Studying hard)으로, ⑤는 While절을 분사구문(Enjoying the sunshine)으로 올바르게 변환했다. ①은 Not knowing, ③은 Living in... (I live -> She lives), ④는 Arriving... (현재 시제 일치 확인 필요) 등의 오류가 있다.
options: ① <u>As I didn't know what to say</u>, I kept silent. → Didn't knowing what to say,
② <u>If you study hard</u>, you'll get A+. → Studying hard,
③ <u>Living in a remote island,</u> she doesn't have any visitors. → Because I live in a remote island,
④ <u>Arriving at the bank</u>, I called him. → When I arrive at the bank,
⑤ <u>While I enjoy the sunshine</u>, I listen to my favorite song. → Enjoying the sunshine,
questions.reason_for_classification: 부사절과 분사구문의 상호 전환 능력을 묻는 문제이다.

questions.passage:
Then one day, a terrible oil spill occurred in the Gulf of Mexico. A lot of sea animals were dying ⓐ<u>since</u> they were completely covered with oil. Carter and Olivia had to do something. They started collecting animal rescue supplies such as pet carrying cages and rubber gloves from everyone in their neighborhood ⓑ<u>for four months</u>. Their family drove to the Gulf of Mexico to deliver animal rescue supplies and helped to save the animals. They learned something very useful ⓒ<u>during</u> they were working there. They put mayonnaise into a turtle’s throat, ⓓ<u>for</u> it could cause turtles to throw up and help to get oil out of them. They said they never knew mayonnaise could be used to save animals!
On their last day, they met a marine life specialist. She told them that plastic waste is more dangerous to sea animals than oil spills are. A lot of sea animals and sea birds die from eating plastic waste. ⓔ<u>Since</u> then they have been doing various educational projects about how to reduce plastic waste and save animals.
questions.question: 13. 위 글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 가장 적절하지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓒ의 during은 전치사이므로 뒤에 주어+동사가 올 수 없다. 접속사인 while이 쓰여야 한다.
questions.reason_for_classification: 전치사 during과 접속사 while의 차이를 구별하는 문제이다.

questions.passage:
In Finland, where it is very cold in winter, people have a special drink when they catch a cold. It is a cup of onion milk. They put chopped onion in milk and boil it over low heat for half an hour. This simple drink is said to be good for a cold.
ⓕ<u>While</u> people in Korea and Finland look for drinks when sick, many people in America want a bowl of chicken soup. It is usually made with chicken and vegetables, but the recipe is different from one family to another. Salt and pepper can be added before eating. People in America believe that a bowl of warm chicken soup is great for a sore throat and a stuffy nose.
In Russia and in Eastern Europe, when people get sick, they eat a dessert called gogol‑mogol. It is made with eggs and honey. Some people add chocolate, butter, lemon juice, or milk to make it taste better. It looks like thick yogurt. People often drink a cup of warm gogol‑mogol when they have a sore throat. Gogol‑mogol is not only good for people with a cold but also popular as a dessert for healthy people. When served as a dessert, it is usually served cold or at room temperature.
questions.question: 14. 위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓕ와 의미가 같은 것은?
questions.explanation: 본문의 ⓕ while은 '~인 반면에'라는 대조의 의미이다. ②번 문장 역시 어제는 비가 온 '반면에' 오늘은 맑다는 대조의 의미이다. ①, ③, ④, ⑤는 '~하는 동안'의 의미이다.
options: ① Don’t bother me <u>while</u> I’m studying.
② <u>While</u> it rained yesterday, it’s sunny today.
③ Jiwu called you <u>while</u> you were taking a shower.
④ Clean the living room <u>while</u> I prepare for dinner.
⑤ <u>While</u> he was sleeping, the window was broken.
questions.reason_for_classification: 접속사 while의 두 가지 주요 의미인 '동안에'와 '반면에'를 구분하는 문제이다.

questions.question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말은?
questions.explanation: 1. 비가 오고 있었기 '때문에' 혹은 '오는 동안', 2. 하진은 축구를 좋아하지만(반면에) 다니엘은 야구를 좋아한다, 3. 하나가 시를 쓰는 '반면에/동안' 미나는 소설을 쓴다. 모두 while이 문법적/의미적으로 어울린다. 특히 대조의 의미가 강하다.
sentences: 1. We decided not to go out ________ it was raining.
2. Hajin likes soccer _______ Daniel likes baseball.
3. _________Hana writes poems, Mina writes novels.
(* 대소문자 관계 없음)
questions.reason_for_classification: 다양한 문맥에서 while의 대조와 시간 용법을 공통적으로 적용할 수 있는지 묻는다.

questions.passage:
What do you do when you catch a cold? Of course, you want to stay warm, so maybe you put on more clothes. Some people like to drink hot tea. Ginger tea is something people in Korea often drink. With its special taste, it warms your body and helps reduce the pain in your throat. What do people drink or eat in other countries when they catch a cold? Let’s find out.
In Finland, where it is very cold in winter, people have a special drink when they catch a cold. It is a cup of onion milk. They put chopped onion in milk and boil it over low heat for half an hour. This simple drink is said to be good for a cold.
(A) <u>While</u> people in Korea and Finland look for drinks when sick, many people in America want a bowl of chicken soup. It is usually made with chicken and vegetables, but the recipe is different from one family to another. Salt and pepper can be added before eating. People in America believe that a bowl of warm chicken soup is great for a sore throat and a stuffy nose.
questions.question: 16. 위 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 쓰임과 가장 다른 것은?
questions.explanation: 본문의 while은 '~인 반면에'라는 의미이다. ①의 while은 '~하는 동안'의 의미로 쓰였다. ②, ③, ④, ⑤는 모두 '반면에/양보'의 의미이다.
options: ① Don’t bother me <u>while</u> I’m studying.
② It’s sunny today <u>while</u> it rained yesterday.
③ <u>While</u> I can ride a bike, I can’t drive a car.
④ My brother is very short <u>while</u> I am very tall.
⑤ <u>While</u> she is good at English, she is not good at math.
questions.reason_for_classification: while의 '동안'과 '반면' 용법을 구별하는 문법성 판단 문제이다.

questions.question: 17. 다음 대화의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓓ는 'for'가 이유를 나타내는 등위접속사로 쓰여 어법상 적절하다. ⓐ exciting -> excited, ⓑ because of it's -> because it's, ⓒ Ms. J를 받는 She는 문장 중간이 아니면 소문자로 시작해야 하거나 문맥상 creative와 연결이 어색하며, ⓔ after I graduate (미래 시제 대신 현재 시제).
sentences: Cheong: How do you feel about becoming a 3rd grader and having our first English exam this year?

questions.question: 35. 다음은 친구들이 Tim에게 남긴 음성사서함 메시지이다. 메시지의 빈칸에 한 번씩만 사용하여 문장을 완성하고자 할 때 사용될 수 없는 것은?

questions.question: 36. 다음 <보기>의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 다음 각 문장의 빈칸에 넣어 완성했을 때, 어법상 가장 적절한 것은?

questions.question: 37. 다음 속담을 설명한 <보기>의 문장 속 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 although가 들어갈 수 있는 곳을 고른 것은?

sentences:

<Korean proverbs and their meanings>

questions.question: 38. ‘so that’의 연결이 어색한 것은?

questions.question: 42. 문장의 전환이 어색한 것은?

questions.passage:
Life with Robots
Where do We See Robots now?
Robots are not only in movies and books anymore. Around the world, robots are doing a variety of tasks. There are delivery robots flying in the sky, robot arms in factories, and service robots in public places.
Robots Are Becoming Smart
In the past, ㉠<u>robots</u> performed only easy tasks that humans programmed them to do. However, robots are now getting “smarter,” and soon they might be able to think like humans. (A)[That / What] makes this possible is artificial intelligence (AI).
㉡<u>Robots</u> that have AI can perceive environments and make decisions. They can also recognize speech, tell jokes, and play games with humans.
AI Speakers: They can answer your questions, control machines in your home, and play music for you.
AI Pets: They act just like real dogs. They walk and play with their owners and recognize praise.
Robots around US – Present and Future
Robots are making things faster and easier. They can help us anywhere – in our homes, on roads, or in disaster areas.
Home Helper Robot: This robot helps your family throughout the day. Cooking and cleaning would be easier if you had one. It also talks with family members and can sense emotions.
Self-Driving Car: A self-driving car doesn’t need a driver. You can relax and enjoy the ride (B)[since / so that] it can navigate roads for you with cameras, sensors, and software.
Robot Swarm: A robot swam is a large group of robots that can communicate with one another, like ants or bees. They can be used in a variety of places, including farms or building sites. They work on tasks and find solutions as a group.
Search-and-Rescue Robot: Search-and-rescue robots can go into disaster areas (C)[which / where] humans can be in danger. They find survivors, deal with dangers, and clear routes so that people can escape to safety.
(가)
Looking toward the Future
Our future with robots looks bright but not perfect. We expect life to become more convenient with the help of robots. However, we also worry about problems they might cause, such as threats to our jobs and safety. All kinds of robots have potential problems that we haven’t thought of. The important thing is to find possible solutions and to ensure that robots are only used for good.
questions.question: 4. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 적절한 것으로만 짝지은 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 뒤에 동사가 오고 선행사가 없으므로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 What이 적절하며, (B)는 뒤에 이유를 나타내므로 since가, (C)는 완전한 문장을 이끄는 관계부사 where가 적절함.
questions.reason_for_classification: 관계대명사 what, 이유의 접속사 since, 관계부사 where의 복합적인 쓰임을 묻는 문법 문제임.

questions.question: 5. 두 문장의 의미가 같지 않은 것은?
questions.explanation: ③에서 'so that she could'를 'in order that they could'로 바꾸면 주어가 she에서 they로 변하여 의미가 일치하지 않음.
options:
① We will practice hard so that we can win the game.
→We will practice hard in order to win the game.

② My sister does exercise every morning so that she/can stay healthy.
→My sister does exercise every morning to stay healthy.

③ She went to the restaurant so that she could have dinner with her family.
→She went to the restaurant in order that they could have dinner with her family.

④ She went to the shop so that she could buy things on sale.
→She went to the shop to buy things on sale.

⑤ Henri got up early so that he could attend the meeting on time.
→Henri got up early in order to attend the meeting on time.
questions.reason_for_classification: 목적을 나타내는 접속사절과 부정사구 간의 전환 시 주어의 일치 여부를 판단하는 문제임.

questions.question: 6. 어법상 틀린 문장은?
questions.explanation: ①에서 'so'는 뒤에 'that'절을 수반하거나 'too ~ to' 구문을 사용해야 하므로 'The suitcase is too large to fit...'이 되어야 함.
options: ① The suitcase is so large to fit in the trunk of my car.
② The book is so thick that I can’t read it in a week.
③ John is so organized that he can arrange a successful event.
④ The mountain was so tall that climbing it seemed impossible.
⑤ Jack is highly experienced enough to care for disabled children.
questions.reason_for_classification: so~that 구문과 too~to 구문의 형태적 혼동 여부를 묻는 문제임.

questions.passage: An Changho was born in 1878. When he was in his teens, he moved to Seoul and went to school there. In 1902, he left for America (A)________ he could get a better education. In America, An helped improve the lives of the Korean people there and became a respected leader. After he (B)_________ to Korea, he founded the New Korean Society in 1907 to fight for Korea’s independence. He also joined the Government of the Republic of Korea in Shanghai in 1919. After that, he built a lot of school to educate people until he died in 1938.
questions.question: 7. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말이 바르게 연결된 것은?
questions.explanation: (A)는 뒤에 절이 오며 목적을 나타내므로 so that이 적절하고, (B)는 과거 사건(독립협회 설립)보다 이전의 일을 나타내거나 과거의 전후 관계를 강조하므로 과거완료 had returned가 적절함.
options: ④ in order to               had returned
⑤ in order that             will return
questions.reason_for_classification: 목적의 접속사 so that과 과거 시점 간의 선후 관계를 나타내는 시제 일치(과거완료)를 묻는 문제임.

questions.question: 8. 주어진 단어를 주어진 우리말에 맞게 배열하시오.
questions.explanation: He recorded her words so that it could be listened to again. 형태의 수동태 구문이나 혹은 'so that he could listen to her words again' 구조가 생각될 수 있으나 주어진 단어(be, it)를 고려할 때 'He recorded her words so that they(it) could be listened to again' 형식의 목적절이 필요함. (주어진 단어 기준: He recorded her words so that it could be listened to again.)
sentences: * 주어진 단어만을 활용할 것.
her / it / so / could / he / listen / recorded / to / that / words / again / be
그는 나중에 다시 듣기 위해서 그녀의 말을 기록하였다.
questions.answer: He recorded her words so that it could be listened to again.
questions.reason_for_classification: 목적의 so that 절 내부에 수동태 구문을 결합하여 문장을 완성하는 서술형 문제임.

questions.question: 9. so, that을 활용하여 주어진 문장과 같은 의미가 되도록 고치시오.
questions.explanation: 'in order not to'는 부정형이므로 so that 절에서는 'so that + 주어 + 조동사부정형'인 'so that he wouldn't miss the bus'가 됨.
sentences: (단. would 활용할 것)
He skipped breakfast in order not to miss the bus.
questions.answer: so that he wouldn't miss the bus
questions.reason_for_classification: 부정의 목적을 나타내는 in order not to를 so that... wouldn't 절로 전환하는 능력을 평가함.

questions.question: 10. 다음의 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 ①~⑤의 단어들을 바르게 배열하여 문장을 완성할 때 ♥에 올 단어는?
questions.explanation: 'so stressed that it takes hours' 어순으로 'Are you so stressed that it takes hours...?' 문장이 완성되므로 ♥ 자리에 올 네 번째 단어는 it임. (어순: stressed(5) - that(3) - it(1) - takes(4))
sentences: 스트레스를 너무 많이 받아서 잠이 들기까지 많은 시간이 걸리는가?
"Are you so _____ _____ __♥___ _____ hours to fall asleep?“
questions.reason_for_classification: so~that 결과 구문과 비인칭 주어 it(시간 소요)이 결합된 복합 어순 문제임.

questions.question: 11. 다음 중 어법상 옳은 문장은?
questions.explanation: ② 'so + 부사 + that' 구문으로 어법상 옳음. ①은 carry 뒤에 목적어 it이 필요하며, ③은 so small a town, ④는 confidently(부사), ⑤는 such an incredible birthday가 되어야 함.
options: ① This package is so heavy that I couldn’t carry.
② He plays so loudly that I can not rest at home.
③ We live in so a small town that we know one another.
④ She spoke so confident that she convinced the entire audience.
⑤ I had so an incredible birthday that I would like to thank you for it.
questions.reason_for_classification: so~that 구문의 어순(so 형/부 a 명) 및 품사의 적절성(형용사 vs 부사), 타동사의 목적어 유무 등을 묻는 종합 문법 문제임.

questions.question: 12. 어법상 옳은 문장의 개수는?
questions.explanation: 옳은 문장: 'I studied hard in order to pass...', 'He was so angry that...', 'When she comes back home, she will...' 3개임. (틀린 것: to hot too -> too hot to, isn't strong so to -> isn't strong enough to, isn't enough big -> isn't big enough)
sentences: • The tea is to hot too drink.
• That box isn't strong so to sit on.
• I studied hard in order to pass the exam.
• He was so angry that he couldn't calm down.
• This car isn't enough big to carry eight people.
• When she comes back home, she will call her dad.
questions.reason_for_classification: too~to, enough to, so~that 및 시간 부사절의 시제 일치 등 다수의 문법 사항을 판별해야 하는 문제임.

questions.question: 13. so, that을 활용하여 주어진 문장과 같은 의미가 되도록 고치시오.
questions.explanation: too~to 부정 구문은 'so + 형용사 + that + 주어 + cannot'으로 전환함. 'His bag is so heavy that it cannot be moved easily.'
sentences: (단. can 활용할 것)
His bag is too heavy to be moved easily.
questions.answer: so heavy that it cannot be moved easily
questions.reason_for_classification: too~to 구문을 so~that절로 전환하는 전형적인 문법 문제임.

questions.passage:

He said, "My flower is (A) <u>so/such</u> real that a bee landed on it." I said, "Drawing on walls (B) <u>was/were</u> much harder than drawing on paper."
We all agreed that our wall painting wasn’t perfect. But it didn’t matter. We made our neighborhood (C) <u>a few/a little</u> brighter and happier. We were proud of ourselves. We didn’t just paint pictures on a wall that day. We painted a better tomorrow!
questions.question: 14. (A), (B), (C)의 각 네모 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 형용사 real 앞이므로 so, (B) 동명사 주어 Drawing은 단수 취급하므로 was, (C) 형용사의 비교급 brighter를 수식하거나 정도를 나타낼 때 '조금'이라는 의미로 a little이 적절함.
questions.reason_for_classification: so~that 구문, 동명사 주어의 수 일치, 수량 형용사/부사(a little)의 쓰임을 묻는 복합 문법 문제임.

questions.question: 15. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 옳은 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓐ 'so + 형용사 + that' 구문이므로 옳음. ⓑ는 than drawing, ⓒ는 didn't matter, ⓓ는 ourselves, ⓔ는 강조구문 It was... that... 혹은 관계사가 불필요하거나 which가 쓰여야 함(여기서는 강조구문 맥락).
questions.reason_for_classification: so~that 구문, 비교 대상의 병렬, 조동사 뒤 동사원형, 재귀대명사의 복수형 등 지문 내 어법 판단력을 묻는 문제임.

questions.question: 16. 다음 중 밑줄 친 as의 뜻이 나머지와 다른 것은?
questions.explanation: ①, ②, ③, ⑤는 모두 '~할 때(시간)'의 의미이지만, ④는 '~했듯이, ~하는 대로(양태)'의 의미임.
options: ① The play started <u>as</u> I got there.
② Don’t use the cellphone <u>as</u> you are driving.
③ <u>As</u> Mom was young, she used to be a fashion model.
④ <u>As</u> I told you, we will meet at 6:00 in front of the bus stop.
⑤ <u>As</u> I looked out the window, I saw a cat running across the yard.
questions.reason_for_classification: 다양한 의미를 지닌 접속사 as의 용법을 구별하는 문제임.

questions.question: 17. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) '~함에 따라' 혹은 '~할 때'의 의미로, (B) 역시 지진 상황의 '때'를 나타내므로 접속사 as가 공통으로 들어갈 수 있음.

questions.passage: Why do I want to buy what my friends bought? Jeff goes to the shopping center and sees a pair of soccer shoes on display. He recognizes the shoes at a glance because more than half of the boys on his soccer team wear them. Although he already has many pairs of soccer shoes, he ends up buying another new pair. We can use the "bandwagon effect" to explain Jeff's behavior. A bandwagon is a wagon in a parade that encourages people to jump aboard and enjoy the music. ⓐ<u>As</u> more and more people get on the bandwagon, others are more likely to get on or follow it. In this way, people tend to buy something just because other people have bought it.
questions.question: 18. 다음 중 밑줄 친 ⓐ와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
questions.explanation: 지문의 ⓐ 'As'는 '~함에 따라(비례)'의 의미임. ③ 역시 '내가 나이 들어감에 따라'라는 비례의 의미로 사용됨. ①은 원급비교, ②는 시간, ④는 가정법(as if), ⑤는 전치사(~로서)임.
options: ① The movie was just <u>as</u> exciting as I expected.
② The kids played outside <u>as</u> the sun began to set.
③ <u>As</u> I grew older, I became more interested in history.
④ He acted <u>as</u> if he didn't know anything about the situation.
⑤ They used the old barn <u>as</u> storage to keep the used things.
questions.reason_for_classification: 비례(~함에 따라)를 나타내는 접속사 as의 용법을 구별하는 문제임.

questions.question: 19. 밑줄 친 말의 쓰임이 다른 하나는?
questions.explanation: ②, ③, ④, ⑤는 모두 '~함에 따라(비례)'의 의미이지만, ①은 '속담/관용구'로서 '~하는 대로(양태)'의 의미임.
options: ① Do <u>as</u> the Romans do when you are in Rome.
② <u>As</u> you make more money, you'll spend more.
③ <u>As</u> people walk more, they become healthier.
④ <u>As</u> he gets richer, he spends more.
⑤ I love you <u>as</u> time goes by.
questions.reason_for_classification: 비례의 as와 양태의 as를 구별하는 문제임.

questions.question: 20. 다음 문장의 밑줄 친 (A)와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
questions.explanation: 제시문의 as는 '~ 때문에(이유)'의 의미임. ③ 역시 피곤했기 때문에라는 이유의 의미로 사용됨. ①은 양태, ②, ④는 전치사, ⑤는 양태임.
options: ① <u>As</u> you know, Julia is leaving soon.
② Does Tom work there <u>as</u> a manager?
③ <u>As</u> Jane was very tired, she went to bed early.
④ He went to the costume party dressed <u>as</u> a banana.
⑤ <u>As</u> the weather forecast predicted, it snowed all day.
sentences: <u>As</u> she had no money, she couldn't buy the dress.
questions.reason_for_classification: 이유를 나타내는 접속사 as의 용법을 식별하는 문제임.

questions.question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ와 어법상 쓰임이 같은 것은?
questions.explanation: 지문의 ⓐ 'as'는 명사 앞의 전치사로서 '~로서(자격)'의 의미임. ② 역시 화병으로서(as a vase)라는 전치사로 사용됨. ①, ⑤는 접속사, ③은 숙어적 부사구, ④는 원급 비교임.

questions.question: 22. 다음 중 어법상 옳은 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
questions.explanation: ⓒ 'as 형/부 as possible' 구문으로 옳음. ⓕ 'built(과거분사구)'가 명사를 수식하므로 옳음. (ⓐ는 talking 혹은 who talked, ⓑ는 three times as old as, ⓓ는 as bad as, ⓔ는 sitting 혹은 who is sitting이 되어야 함.)

questions.question: 23. 다음 중 어색한 문장은 모두 몇 개 인가?
questions.explanation: 모두 틀렸으므로 5개임. 1. as... as, 2. as famous as, 3. not as difficult as, 4. were killed, 5. was taken.

questions.question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 말로 적절한 것은?

In sports, only the players get a trophy or medal, but they don't win on their own. There are people who help the players. These people are often hidden and don't get attention. However, they are as important as the players. Here are some examples.
Pacers in a Marathon
Pacers run with other runners and lead them in a marathon. ⓐ<u>Pacers are experienced runners, and their job is to help other runners manage their race better</u>. There can be several pacers in a race. Each pacer runs at different speeds and finishes the race in different times. ⓑ<u>Pacers usually have flags or balloons showing their finish time</u>.
Runners can choose a pacer depending on their target finish time. For example, if a runner wants to finish the race in four hours, the runner will follow the four-hour pacer. ⓒ<u>Since the pacer keeps track of the time, the runner can achieve his or her goal of finishing the marathon in a particular time more easily</u>. In short, pacers run but they don't run to win. (A)______________________________Pit_Crews_in_Car_Racing

A pit is a place on the side of the race track, and drivers stop there several times during a race.
